findings.consequence: The page's only art section, which is its principal visual content, reads as an unfinished grid at tablet width. The three-work set breaks apart, and a large black void lands in the middle of the page.
findings.change: Keep the three works in one row from the md breakpoint (768px) up, at about 215px per column at 820 with captions wrapping. Alternatively, use any tablet arrangement that leaves no empty grid cell. Keep object-contain and the current 1440 and 390 layouts.
findings.acceptance_check: At 820x1000 all three works sit in one balanced arrangement with no empty grid cell beside a work. Images keep their aspect ratios, captions are unclipped, and the 1440x1000 and 390x844 captures are unchanged.

findings.observation: 'How the Museum works' and 'The next stage' are adjacent sections with identical peer dividers (1px top rule, 112px gap), but they are built differently. 'How the Museum works' has an eyebrow, a 36px H2 in the left column, and three cards in a two-column grid inside the right column, so 'Rights education' sits alone beside an empty cell at 1440 and 820. 'The next stage' has no eyebrow, a 30px H2 (24px at 390, where its peers are 30px), a full-width stacked heading, and a full-width three-up row starting at x=170, not x=653. 'How the Museum works' also takes 56px top padding where its siblings take 40px at 768px and up. Round 01: every peer H2 measures 36px at 1440 and 820 and 30px at 390. 'The next stage' uses the heading-left split, both groups stack as one column starting at x=653 at 1440 with no empty cell, and every peer section has 40px top padding. Round 02: unchanged. automated-checks.json records 40px top padding and a 1px top border on every peer section at all three widths.
findings.consequence: Readers cannot tell whether 'The next stage' is a peer topic or a continuation of 'How the Museum works'. The two parallel three-item groups do not line up, and the empty cell beside 'Rights education' reads as a missing item. The institutional half of the page looks assembled rather than designed.
findings.change: Decide the relationship and express it once. (a) As a peer, give 'The next stage' the same H2 size and heading-left split as its siblings. (b) As a subsection, nest it inside 'How the Museum works' without the peer divider and 112px gap, with a clearly subordinate heading. Either way, lay out both three-item groups on one grid, either three columns or a single stacked column within the right column, with no empty cell. Use the sibling 40px top padding.
findings.acceptance_check: At 1440, 820, and 390, every peer section H2 renders at one size, or 'The next stage' visibly sits inside 'How the Museum works' with no peer divider. At 1440 the two three-item groups share one left edge and column count, and no grid cell beside 'Rights education' is empty at 1440 or 820.

findings.observation: Each work title is an inline-flex link with a 44px minimum height and vertically centered text (tw-min-h-11 tw-items-center). One-line titles (CENTURY #31, CENTURY #724) therefore sit about 10px lower than the first line of the two-line 'Patrolling the border between the Negev Desert and Jordan' (text tops at y≈1084 and y≈1074 at 1440). The title-to-artist gap is about 14px under a one-line title but 4px under the two-line title. The artist lines (y 1122 and 1126) and the bottom rules (y 1158 and 1162) step by 4px across the row. At 390 the stacked captions visibly use two different title-to-artist spacings. Round 01: the three titles' first-line tops are all y=1077 at 1440 and y=947 at 820, and each artist line sits 8px below its title's last line at all three widths. Round 02: unchanged. In evidence/about-1440x1000-02.png the three titles still start on one line.
findings.consequence: The caption row, the most museum-specific typographic element on the page, looks unaligned, and identical caption roles get different spacing depending on title length.
findings.change: Keep the 44px target but top-align the title text, for example with tw-items-start, or by moving the minimum height to a padded block or hit-area pseudo-element, so every title's first line starts at the caption top. Keep a constant 4px gap from a title's last line to the artist line.
findings.acceptance_check: At 1440 the first-line tops of the three titles match within 1px. At every viewport, each artist line sits the same distance below its title's last line in all three captions.

findings.observation: At 1440 the hero's lead paragraph runs about 95 characters per line (896px wide at 20px), and its second paragraph about 110. Right-column body copy at 16px runs about 90-95 characters (698px). At 820, single-column body copy and the grey 'The next stage' card text run about 95 characters across 692px. Round 01: the hero lead is 723px at 20px (about 72 characters per line), and section paragraphs are capped at 578px (about 45-80 characters per line). Round 02: the four edited paragraphs stay at 578px and 16px at 1440 and 820 in the running build. They wrap to 136/2, 162/2, 135/2, and 246/4 characters per line, so the longest line is about 81 characters, in the 'Public record' card, and every other line is about 68 or fewer.
findings.consequence: Long lines slow reading and make return sweeps error-prone in the passages that explain what the Museum is, the core of this page's task.
findings.change: Cap reading paragraphs at about 65-75ch, for example with tw-max-w-prose or tw-max-w-[68ch] on hero and section paragraphs, or a hero text max width of about 720px. Leave headings and link rows as they are.
findings.acceptance_check: At 1440x1000 and 820x1000 no reading paragraph on the route exceeds about 80 characters per line, measured from the captures. 390x844 is unchanged.

findings.observation: The page ends with three link groups. 'Institutional sources' lists Founding record, Open Museum statement, On-chain transition, Museum Safe, and View the public record. Next come the 'Source and contribute' links. Last is a 12px grey disclosure, 'Related works and context', and when opened in the running build it reveals only 'On-chain transition' and 'Founding principles', both already linked about 150px above. Round 01: the running build has no details element at any width, and 'Institutional sources' lists Founding principles, The Open Museum statement, and On-chain transition, each URL once. Round 02: unchanged. The running build has zero details elements at all three widths, and the page end matches evidence/about-1440x1000-05.png, evidence/about-820x1000-06.png, and evidence/about-390x844-09.png.
findings.consequence: Visitors spend a click to find nothing new, and the same document under two labels ('Founding record' and 'Founding principles') suggests two different records, which blurs where the authoritative source lives.
findings.change: On this route, drop the related-context items that already appear in 'Institutional sources', and do not render the disclosure when nothing remains. Alternatively, list only genuinely related works or pages that are not linked elsewhere on the page.
findings.acceptance_check: At all three widths, each document URL at the page end appears once in 'Institutional sources' (apart from the page's own 'Read the source' link), and no disclosure on the route expands to only links already shown on the page.
